{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and the clock is running. A fish is easy to read from its outline and its tail fin, and one run from the tail tip can trace it. I'll take the pad and sketch it now so the others can trace it.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish! The tail fin will make it read clearly. I've got the pad and I'm sketching the outline now. Stroke one starts at the top of the tail, so whoever's free, get ready to trace it.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [3, 5],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[3,5],[5,8],[7,8.5],[11,7],[16,6.8],[20,8],[22,10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[22,10],[20,12],[16,13.2],[11,13],[7,11.5],[5,12]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[5,12],[2,15]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 18, "y": 9, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Animal: fish facing right. START at top tip of tail (3,5). Stroke 1 = top edge from tail to nose. Stroke 2 = bottom edge back from nose. Stroke 3 = lower tail fin branching off end of stroke 2. I hold the pad. Next: have Omar or Jack trace stroke 1 first, then others trace 2 and 3 and fix gaps."
